comparison_note: Map semantic/RGB metrics compare only shared spatial cells; topology metrics separately measure cells added or removed. Downstream token metrics compare corresponding block queries or fixed global latent indices.

learned_query_diversity.note: The learned query parameters are diverse, but their output native latents collapse to mean off-diagonal cosine 0.9999944. The shared global context overwhelms query diversity.

summary_findings.diagnosis: The counterfactual signal is present in raw and aggregated maps and remains visible in spatial block tokens. The dominant loss occurs in the global Perceiver resampler: its 256 native latents are almost duplicate vectors, and scene-pair relative L2 falls by roughly two to three further orders of magnitude before LM projection. Distinct SHA-256 hashes therefore certify only bitwise inequality, not a behaviorally useful separation.
summary_findings.recommended_fix: Preserve spatially anchored latent diversity, add an explicit paired counterfactual scene-token separation/diversity objective, and keep or amplify projected scene differences above the float16 quantization floor before injecting them into the frozen language model.

corroborating_control_results.interpretation: Wrong-scene, shuffled-semantic, shuffled-position, and geometry-only controls match or slightly exceed primary exact accuracy, while primary changed-fact consistency is zero. This corroborates a learned near-constant soft-prompt/prior solution rather than effective use of scene-specific signal.

purpose: Counterfactual signal audit from numeric maps through frozen-LM behavior
